narratives.Overview:
1. For the same-owner rebase path (session id, worktree, and scope unchanged; actor already owns the live lease): extend the existing owner-gated ritual HEAD continuity seam so a legitimate rebase / discontinuous HEAD does not permanently revoke write/search_replace for the remainder of the run. Prefer extending evaluateLoadedState / rebindForwardHead / assessRearmEligibility / writeRitualStateIfStillOwned under live-same-owner admit — not a greenfield --rebind-head verb and not #3117 freshness:bind (generation/payload, not git_head).
2. Keep discontinuous HEAD fail-closed for foreign history rewrite (branch-switch / amend / stranger HEAD) per #2782. Continuity is for the same-owner rebase/ff case the merge path requires, not unbound ritual rewrite.
3. Split occupancy limbs: same-owner cold / session:ready is already envelope-legal occupancy-wise (live-same-owner admit + heartbeat). Foreign live owner, granted-member, and cancelled-predecessor residue stay parent-owned lease hygiene or owner rebind — not worker steal/impersonation. Do not bind "no occupancy touch ever" as the sole universal remedy.
4. Denial / recovery copy: re-anchor operator-facing discontinuous-HEAD recovery on current #4290 composition (unauthorized ceremony verbs stripped when occupancy refuses; same-owner names a recovery the owner can run). Do not leave Stop 1 P2 wording that assumes every discontinuous-HEAD denial still advertises session:start when the actor cannot claim.
5. Tests + CHANGELOG: HEAD-discontinuity rebind / continuity for unchanged session+worktree+same-owner lease; keep #2782 fail-closed cases. Distinct from #3873 / #3877 / #3861 / #4291.

issueCommentThread.body:
Adoption blocker.

This is about Continuity: closing the laptop and coming back, or handing the work to another session, using only what was written down. When something gets stuck, the recovery on screen should work.

What a new person hits: Updating a branch onto a moved main branch takes away the agent's permission to edit. The recovery printed on screen requires a lock the agent is not allowed to take.

Why that ruins the product for them: A normal git update locks the work, and the suggested fix is illegal. They are stuck for doing the right git thing.

How likely: Medium. It needs a branch that has moved, which is common as soon as they pull or rebase.

design-critique: warranted, because a required rebase onto moved master invalidates ritual HEAD binding and kills write/search_replace for the same worker, while the printed recovery (session:start / session:ready) claims occupancy the envelope forbids the worker to take or steal.

charter: refutation
refutation-target: After a legitimate rebase that moves git HEAD, it is acceptable that the worker lose edit authority for the rest of the run, because the printed recovery is a full session:start / session:ready cold ceremony that claims occupancy — even when session id, worktree, and scope are unchanged and the envelope forbids lease take/steal.

Recommended spend N=1. Eval noted needs-re-scope against completed #4291 brief; #4291 is a different primary-checkout/branch-signal defect and does not close this rebase/rebind hole.

pain: P1, P2, P3

P1. A drive-to: merge-ready worker that rebases onto moved master loses write / search_replace for the remainder of the run (ritual HEAD discontinuity / stale ritual state denial).
P2. The printed recovery names session:start / session:ready, which claim the worktree occupancy lease; the dispatch envelope forbids taking, releasing, or impersonating a lease the worker does not own, so the denied actor has no envelope-legal recovery.
P3. Compliant edits are blocked while an equivalent uncontrolled path (e.g. PowerShell WriteAllText) stays open — same shape as neighboring gate-bypass reports.

Inventory at the pin (before any new mechanism): `verify-session-ritual.ts` `headDriftRecoveryMessage` + `gitIsAncestor` forward rebind (`rebindForwardHead`); `session-start.ts` `assessRearmEligibility` refuses discontinuous HEAD; `branches.test.ts` locks forward-commit stay-fresh and branch-switch/amend fail-closed (#2782); `occupancy.ts` `evaluateOccupancyCeremonyEligibility` (`live-same-owner` admits; `live-foreign-owner` / `granted-member` refuse owner claim); `occupancy-recovery.ts` #4290 strips unauthorized `session:ready` / `session:start` when ceremony is refused; hook path occupancy-before-ritual (#3769) with `writeRitualStateIfStillOwned`; `freshness:bind` is generation/payload (#3117), not git HEAD. No `--rebind-head` verb. Related #4291 is a different primary-checkout/branch-signal defect.

Injection / swarm lens: ritual-state and worktree occupancy are shared authority. Any discontinuous-HEAD rebind must stay under the live owner write path (`writeRitualStateIfStillOwned` after occupancy admit). An unbound HEAD rewrite would reopen the #3769 class where a denied actor retitles the owner's ritual.

## Same-owner cold recovery does not require steal
sharpens-framing
Evidence: At `650ab1a614cd6049b4c70c2b48fa181ffef5455e`, `evaluateOccupancyCeremonyEligibility` returns `admitCeremony: true` for `live-same-owner`; `applyWorktreeOccupancy` heartbeats the same session id rather than stealing. Hook denials that reach `headDriftRecoveryMessage` already passed occupancy; `#4290` then appends `formatRitualRecoveryInstruction("cold")` naming `session:ready`. Foreign live owner and granted-member cases refuse ceremony and strip those verbs (`occupancy-stale-ritual-recovery.test.ts`).
Failure mode: Binding the target as one package — permanent mid-run loss is fine because recovery always claims a lease the envelope forbids — overfits the cancelled-predecessor story onto the same-owner rebase path, where cold / `session:ready` is already envelope-legal occupancy-wise without take/steal.
Disposition: Split occupancy limbs before bind. Same-owner: owner-gated ritual HEAD refresh under the existing lease. Foreign / member / cancelled-predecessor residue: parent-owned lease hygiene or owner rebind, not a worker steal. Do not treat "no occupancy touch ever" as the sole universal remedy.

## Discontinuous HEAD fail-closed already has a continuity seam
sharpens-framing
Evidence: Pin `assessRearmEligibility` reason `git HEAD changed discontinuously (full cold session:start required)`; `evaluateLoadedState` only rebinds when `gitIsAncestor(pinned, current)`; `#2782` test title and body keep rebase/amend/branch-switch fail-closed while forward commits stay fresh. `freshness:bind` compares deposit generation, not `git_head`.
Failure mode: A greenfield `--rebind-head` or a freshness-axis patch would ignore the existing forward-rebind / re-arm refusal seam and risk unbound ritual authority on rewritten history.
Disposition: Prefer extending the owner-gated ritual HEAD continuity path (when session id + worktree + scope are unchanged and the actor already owns the lease) rather than inventing a parallel verb or routing through `#3117` freshness.

## Pre-#4290 denial text is not the pin-SHA printed recovery for illegal ceremony
footnote
Evidence: Issue body quotes the bare `headDriftRecoveryMessage`. At this SHA, `applyOccupancyEligibilityToDenial` rewrites unauthorized ceremony commands for `live-foreign-owner` / `granted-member` and substitutes occupancy remediation plus `SHELL_COVERAGE_HONESTY`.
Failure mode: None for bind anatomy; the Stop 1 P2 narrative can overstate that discontinuous-HEAD denials still advertise `session:start` when the actor cannot claim.
Disposition: Re-anchor P2 wording on current `#4290` composition when the successor lean cites denial text.

metadata.issueBody:
## Summary

A `drive-to: merge-ready` worker must rebase when master moves under it. Rebasing revokes its own file-edit tools, and the printed recovery is unavailable to it.

From ~19:55Z on 2026-08-28, every `write` / `search_replace` from a worker in its own worktree was denied:

```text
Directive denied write: session ritual state is stale because git HEAD changed
discontinuously. Run `deft session:start` again (full cold ceremony required).
```

Master moved twice during that run. The worker rebased both times -- which the merge path requires -- and after each rebase its edit tools were dead for the remainder of the run.

## Why the recovery is not available

The denial names `session:start` / `session:ready`. Running either **claims the worktree occupancy lease**. In the observed case the lease was held by the worker's own cancelled predecessor, and every dispatch envelope forbids taking, releasing or impersonating a lease it does not own. A worker that follows its envelope therefore has no recovery, and a worker that recovers has violated it.

The result is that the framework's own required action -- rebase before merge -- revokes the actor's authority, and the documented remedy is closed to the actor.

## Distinct from the neighbouring issues

- **#3873** is about actor resolution: the gate cannot determine who is calling. Here the actor resolves fine; a HEAD change invalidates the ritual binding.
- **#3877** is the ambient `DEFT_SESSION_ID` contradiction. Unrelated; this fires with the variable unset.
- **#3861** is release-lag verification for a different denial class.

## Observed twice, by different workers

Both workers finished their runs by routing every edit through PowerShell `[System.IO.File]::WriteAllText`, which the hook does not intercept. That is the same shape recorded on #3873: the gate blocks the compliant path and leaves an equivalent uncontrolled path open.

## Direction (not prescriptive)

A ritual binding invalidated by a legitimate rebase needs a re-bind that does not require a lease transition -- the worker still holds the same worktree, the same identity, and the same scope; only `git_head` moved. Options seen from outside: re-bind on HEAD change when the session id and worktree are unchanged; treat a fast-forward or rebase of the same branch as continuity rather than discontinuity; or provide a `--rebind-head` verb that refreshes the binding without touching occupancy.

Whatever the mechanism, a worker doing what the merge path requires should not end up with fewer capabilities than when it started.

## Acceptance

- [ ] A worker that rebases its own worktree onto a moved master keeps its edit authority
- [ ] If a re-bind is required, it is available without claiming, releasing or stealing an occupancy lease
- [ ] The denial text names a recovery the denied actor can actually perform
- [ ] A test covers HEAD-discontinuity re-bind for an unchanged session and worktree
- [ ] CHANGELOG `[Unreleased]` entry

## Refs

#3873, #3877, #3861, #3613, and the 2026-08-28 worker reports on #3768 and #3607.
